722:
Any owner or operator of any nature recreational facility located or to be located within the county shall be required to obtain a permit from the office of planning and zoning of the county. The term "nature recreational facilities" shall mean any facility which offers to the public outdoor recreational activities, including, but not necessarily limited to, nature trails, bicycle trails, equestrian trails, including those which result from the abandonment of railroad rights-of-way under federal law, as well as all other such nature recreational facilities as may be within the above definition, regardless of the zoning district or districts in which such nature recreational facilities are located.
(Ord. of 9-17-2001)
723:
(a) The application for a nature recreational facility permit shall be submitted to the planning and zoning department of the county. The application shall be accompanied by a non-refundable nature recreational facility permit application fee of $500.00. Said application fee shall be required only in connection with the initial nature recreational facility permit application, and shall not be required for any subsequent renewal as specified in subsection 34-202(b). The planning and zoning department shall issue such permit so long as all fees are paid and the permit complies with the provisions of section 34-203. The planning and zoning department shall have a period not to exceed 60 days in which to approve or disapprove of the permit application. If no action is taken by the planning and zoning department upon the permit application within such 60-day period, then the permit shall be deemed granted. In the event that the application for a nature recreational facility permit is denied, notice of and reasons for the denial thereof shall be provided to the applicant for the permit, and such applicant may file a request for reconsideration with the planning and zoning department within ten days after receipt of notice of such denial. In the event the application is denied upon reconsideration, such applicant may appeal such denial to the board of commissioners of the county within 20 days after receipt of notice of such denial, and the board of commissioners will hold a hearing on such appeal within 15 days after receipt of notice of such appeal. At such hearing, the applicant shall be authorized to present any relevant evidence it desires to present in defense of or mitigation with respect to the matter before the board of commissioners.
(b) Each owner or operator of a nature recreational facility located within the county shall be required to prepare every two years a review application, detailing the nature recreational facility's fulfillment of its requirements as set forth under the provisions of section 34-203. Said review application shall not require a processing fee or any other fee, and shall be due December 31 of each odd numbered year. If at the time of filing the review application the requirements of section 34-203 are not satisfied, the permit of the nature recreational facility may be subject to suspension or revocation by the county commission pursuant to subsection 34-205(b). In such a situation, the procedures governing the suspension or revocation of the permit set forth in section 34-205 shall govern.
(Ord. of 9-17-2001)
724:
No such nature recreational facility permit shall be granted unless the following requirements are met by the applicant at or before the time that the permit is issued:
(1) The owner or operator of the nature recreational facility shall provide written proof that it has in effect, or that it is exempted by federal or state law from having in effect, public liability insurance in connection with the operation of such nature recreational facility, and that such insurance is for a term running concurrent with the permit term.
(2) The owner or operator of the nature recreational facility shall submit plans, specifications, and drawings with respect to the location and dimensions of the proposed nature recreational facility.
(3) Proof that public permanent restrooms shall be located at points along the proposed nature recreation facility not less than every two miles. The permanent public restrooms shall be fixtures attached to the underlying real property. Composting toilets shall be permitted so long as they comply with the standards of the National Sanitation Foundation. In the event that the county's water and sewer system provides service within 150 feet of the site of any such restroom, such restroom facility shall be connected to the county's water and sewer system. Upon notice to the county administrator's office of upcoming special events, and upon approval by the county administrator of an application by the nature recreational facility owner or operator within 15 days of such special events, portable restroom facilities may be available in conjunction with such special events. Portable restroom facilities, however, shall be available only for temporary use in conjunction with such events.
(4) No lighting of any kind shall be installed at any point along the nature recreational facility, except at trail heads.
(5) Proof that the owner or operator will provide, at its sole cost and expense, receptacles for litter and trash along the nature recreational facility, as well as provide for the cleaning of litter not deposited in the trash receptacles along the nature recreational facility.
(6) Placement at each point of public access of signs listing the prohibitions contained in section 34-204.
(7) Each public road crossing a nature recreation facility as defined in section 34-201 of this Code shall be at grade unless otherwise approved by the Lee County Board of Commissioners. The approval of any exception to this requirement at a particular grade crossing shall be solely based upon extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular crossing because of its size, shape, or topography and a finding by the board of commissioners that such conditions are peculiar to the subject grade crossing.
(8) Any nature recreational facilities as defined in section 34-201 which are constructed primarily for human traffic and not for animal or bicycle traffic, shall be constructed of class A concrete and shall be a minimum of ten feet wide and a maximum of 12 feet wide unless otherwise approved by the Lee County Board of Commissioners. The approval of any exception to this requirement shall be solely based upon extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to area of the trail subject to the exception request because of its size, shape, or topography and a finding by the board of commissioners that such conditions are peculiar to the area of the trail subject to the exception request.
(Ord. of 9-17-2001; Ord. of 5-28-2013; Ord. of 10-22-2019)
725:
No person shall, while using said nature recreational facility, do or engage in any of the following activities:
(1) Possess, use, consume, or drink any alcoholic beverages at any time on the nature recreational facility property.
(2) Possess, use, or consume any controlled substances (illegal drugs) at any time on the nature recreational facility property.
(3) Engage in overnight camping on the nature recreational facilities; nor shall there be any motorized vehicles, including motorcycles, permitted or allowed on the nature recreational facilities at any time, with the exception of emergency vehicles or service vehicles used for trail maintenance.
(4) Possess or use any weapons of any type at any time on the nature recreational facility property.
(5) Have in his or her possession, or set off or otherwise cause to explode, discharge, or burn, or throw onto property adjacent to such nature recreational facility, any type of fireworks or explosives or inflammable material. This prohibition includes any substance, compound, or mixture article that in conjunction with any other substance or compound would be dangerous from any of the foregoing standpoints.
(6) Build or attempt to build any fire on the nature recreational facility property, and no person shall drop, throw, or otherwise scatter lighted matches, burning cigarettes or cigars, tobacco, paper, or other inflammable material, within the confines of the nature recreational facility or on any property adjacent thereto.
(7) Sleep thereon or engage in loud, boisterous, threatening, abusive, insulting, or indecent language or engage in any disorderly conduct or behavior tending to be a breach of the public peace as to persons on said nature recreational facility or persons residing, passing, or owning property adjacent thereto.
(8) Expose or offer for sale any article or thing, nor shall anyone station or place any stand, cart, or vehicle for the transportation, sale, or display of any article or thing on the nature recreational facilities except such items as may be sold by the owner or operator or its licensees in compliance with county ordinances.
(9) No person shall travel upon any nature trail at any time after dusk and before sunrise on any given day except those persons engaged in trail maintenance activities.
(Ord. of 9-17-2001)
726:
(a) Any person, firm, corporation, partnership, or other entity violating the provisions of section 34-204 above shall be subject to prosecution for violation of county ordinances and, upon conviction thereof, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be subject to the penalties provided in section 1-12 of this Code.
(b) Failure of any permit holder to maintain compliance with section 34-203 shall subject the nature recreational facility permit to potential suspension or revocation. The county commission shall notify the owner or operator of the nature recreational facility of any violations of said section with instructions to cure such violations within 30 days. If such violations are not cured within the time mandated by this provision, and such violations result in continued and systematic violations of said section, the county commission shall be authorized to suspend or revoke the nature recreational facility permit previously issued to the owner or operator thereof after notice and hearing upon such proposed suspension or revocation. A nature recreational facility owner or operator shall be given at least 30 days notice of any such hearing and shall be afforded an opportunity, at such hearing, to present any relevant evidence it desires to present in defense of or mitigation with respect to the matter before the county commission.
(Ord. of 9-17-2001)
727:

731:
The Legislature of the state has in Georgia Code Annotated, Article IX, Section II, delegated the responsibility to local governmental units to adopt regulations designed to promote the public health, safety, and general welfare of its citizenry. Therefore, the board of commissioners does ordain as follows.
(Ord. of 8-27-2009)
732:
(a) The flood hazard areas of Lee County, Georgia are subject to periodic inundation which results in loss of life and property, health and safety hazards, disruption of commerce and governmental services, extraordinary public expenditures for flood relief and protection, and impairment of the tax base, all of which adversely affect the public health, safety and general welfare.
(b) These flood losses are caused by the occupancy in flood hazard areas of uses vulnerable to floods, which are inadequately elevated, floodproofed, or otherwise unprotected from flood damages, and by the cumulative effect of obstructions in floodplains causing increases in flood heights and velocities.
(Ord. of 8-27-2009)
735:
In all special flood hazard areas (SFHA) as shown on the [flood] insurance rate maps (FIRM), the following provisions apply:
(1) New construction of principal buildings (both residential and nonresidential), including manufactured homes, shall not be allowed if any portion of the structure lies within the limits of the "floodway."
(2) All structures to be located within the 100-year zone "AE" floodplain boundaries or 500-year gray shaded zone "X" floodplain boundaries immediately adjacent to the 100-year zone "AE" shall have approved plans for the construction of such structure that evidences that such structure shall be located upon a lot having a minimum of two acres of land legally subdivided prior to a building permit being issued. All structures located in the 100-year zone "AE" floodplain boundaries shall have the first finished floor elevated to at least three feet above the 100-year base flood elevation. All structures located in the 500-year gray shaded zone "X" floodplain boundaries immediately adjacent to the 100-year zone "AE" shall have the first finished floor elevated to at least one foot above the 100-year zone "AE" base flood elevation. An official elevation certificate shall be submitted at time of building permit application attesting to the fact that the finished floor elevation shall be at least at or above the required elevation.
Exemption: An owner of any lot already legally subdivided and approved by October 1, 2005 will be allowed to apply for a building permit under the relevant applicable provisions for construction on such lot that were applicable immediately prior to October 1, 2005. If a building permit is issued under the provisions of this exemption, a structure may be built in the floodplain under such provisions relating to such construction as were applicable immediately prior to October 1, 2005, providing the construction meets all of the other requirements for then-existing development procedures for construction under the floodplain development ordinance of the county.
(Ord. of 8-27-2009)
